bull.b: Consistent, high free cash flow generation provides durable funding for reinvestment, M&A, and shareholder returns. Over 80% FCF conversion of earnings supports sustained capital deployment and reduces reliance on external financing, bolstering long-term financial resilience.

A business model anchored in consumables, reagents, services and software creates sticky, repeatable revenue streams. Installed-base-driven purchases and recurring contracts provide predictable demand and margin support, enhancing revenue visibility and long-term customer retention.

Manageable leverage and demonstrated access to long-term, low-cost financing preserve strategic optionality. The ability to issue multi-year notes while maintaining covenants supports M&A, buybacks and working capital needs without materially stressing the capital structure over the medium term.

bear.b: A multi-year step-down in top-line growth and normalized profitability reduces earnings leverage and long-term return on invested capital. Slower revenue expansion constrains organic growth optionality and means future EPS gains may rely more on M&A or aggressive cost actions to restore prior margin levels.

Large customer shipment timing can create multi-quarter revenue rebasings and reduce visibility. In bioprocessing, delayed capital and consumable orders can defer downstream recurring consumable demand, making near-term growth lumpy and complicating capacity and inventory planning.

Reduced respiratory testing volumes materially affect mix and revenue growth in diagnostics, pressuring margins where higher-margin non-respiratory volumes may not fully offset declines. Prolonged lower respiratory demand could dampen segment growth and constrain near-term margin expansion.
